newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end markedly lower in low volumes.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end markedly lower in low volumes.

text.p: Swiss shares followed weak European bourses to close slightly off the day's lows due to insecurity ahead of Tuesday's U.S. FOMC meeting and a fall in Swiss index heavyweights Ciba, Sandoz, Roche and Nestle.
Volumes were described as below average. Also, last Friday's expiry of September contracts on futures and options exchange Soffex triggered sells, dealers said.
U.S. and British investors were among the sellers, a dealer noted.
Blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) fell 59.4 points, or 1.61 percent, to 3,636.4 points.
All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) gave up 34.13 points, or 1.44 percent, to 2,334.28 points.
Ciba and Sandoz were depressed by concerns their merger as Novartis may be delayed until next year because a U.S. cartel review may take longer than expected.
Sandoz slipped 30 francs to 1,459, Ciba registereds fell 29 francs to 1,555. Roche certificates slid 190 francs to 8,995 francs.

Food giant Nestle was also weak, giving up 22 francs to 1,366 francs. The shares continued a downward trend since the company 10 days ago announced first half-year net profit rose 20 percent year-on-year.
Holderbank slumped almost three percent to 887. A dealer said half-year results were disappointing and the outlook not encouraging.

Holderbank said Monday that group net profit fell 7.5 percent in the first half. It also said 1996 results would at best only reach 1995 levels due to weak European economies and poor weather for European construction at the start of the year.
Quality inspection group Surveillance fell 2.64 percent to 2,765 francs following Friday's release of half year figures.
CS Holding fell one percent, Zurich slumped two percent.
